subject: health
unitTitle: Safety, Injury Prevention, and Emergency Response
title: Explicit model: CPR and AED awareness: what they are, when they are used, and how to get trained
focus: CPR and AED awareness: what they are, when they are used, and how to get trained
essentialQuestion: If something goes wrong in front of me, what do I actually do in the first two minutes?
materials: paper and pencil or an accessible response tool
the fictional lesson cards included in this task
keyPoints: CPR supports circulation and an AED analyzes heart rhythm and may deliver a shock; awareness is not certification, so learners should use current hands-on training and dispatcher guidance.
Classify urgency from observable facts, protect scene safety, activate trained help, and stay within current training rather than attempting an unsafe rescue.
